maya: Heads-up — seeing repeated stalls on IPv6 egress from APAC edge nodes to a handful of CDNs. Clients report slow responses and retries; IPv4 path via NAT64 looks fine.

devin: Which CDN(s)? any reproducible request logs?

maya: Mostly to cdn-fast.example.net (AAAA records present). Capture shows lots of dup ACKs and retransmits on native v6 path. Example tcpdump excerpt: 

```
12:34:56.789 IP6 2601:xxxx:edge:a > 2001:db8:cdn::1: Flags [P.], seq 1:1401, ack 1, win 64240, length 1400
12:34:56.790 IP6 2001:db8:cdn::1 > 2601:xxxx:edge:a: ICMP6 Packet Too Big, mtu=1280
12:35:00.123 IP6 2601:xxxx:edge:a > 2001:db8:cdn::1: Flags [P.], seq 1:1401, ack 1, retransmission
```

maya: Notably DF-equivalent behaviour -> PMTU/MTU issues, and some middleboxes appear to drop ICMPv6 PTB or not forward them back to us.

sasha: Do we have conntrack/hairpinning in the egress path? I've seen flows that go out and back through same LB which can break MTU negotiation.

liam: We also saw similar symptoms before when tcp_mtu_probing was off and a middlebox dropped PTBs. What are current sysctl settings on affected nodes?

maya: Current canary node sysctls: 
```
net.ipv6.conf.all.mc_forwarding=0
net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0
net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=0
```

ben: Quick mitigation options: enable tcp_mtu_probing=1/2 on kernel and add MSS clamping on egress for IPv6. Also consider explicit TCPMSS rule in mangle table for SYNs.

ops-bot: Incident created: INF-APAC-1768 - "ipv6 egress stalls to cdn-fast". Paging oncall.

oncall-bot: @oncall-engineer alerted (priority P2). Please acknowledge in 10m.

maya: Did a tiny canary: enabled net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=2 and applied MSS clamp on two edge nodes. Observed retransmit rate drop ~80% and client errors dropped.

maya: MSS clamp we used: 
```
# IPv6 TCPMSS clamp for SYN packets
ip6tables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --set-mss 1220
```

liam: IPV6 + TCPMSS in mangle is fine, but watch CPU if many flows. Also check if our LB (edgelb) rewrites or does proxying — proxy-mode might bypass kernel mangle rules.

devin: Also verify if upstream CDNs are filtering ICMPv6 PTB. If they are, we cannot rely on PTB; MSS clamp is the safer long-term mitigation.

sasha: Rollout plan suggestion: 1) Enable tcp_mtu_probing=1 on all APAC canaries (low risk). 2) Add MSS clamp at LB level for IPv6 only. 3) Monitor tcp retransmit rate, p50/p95 latency, client error rate for 30m. 4) If stable, roll to rest of APAC, then global.

ben: Config snippet for edgelb annotation (k8s LB) — set annotation to apply sysctl or iptables on node ingress pods, or use host-level init script. Example: 
```
service.beta.kubernetes.io/edgelb-ipv6-mss: "1220"
```
(placeholder — actual implementation will be via DaemonSet applying ip6tables rule).

maya: I'll do the canary tonight at 00:30 UTC per ops window. Will post results here.

devin: If we still see dropped PTB ICMPs after clamp, we should capture pcap across LBs + upstream to prove middlebox behavior and open support ticket with CDN.

oncall-bot: Acknowledged by @oncall-engineer.

maya: Quick note — MSS clamp fixed most cases in canary but one CDN POP still had sporadic stalls; opened a ticket with them and attached packet captures.

sasha: Good. Add alert for sudden increase in icmp6_ptb_rx (if we can surface that) and for SYN retransmit rate.

maya: Will update runbook and add the two-step rollback: remove ip6tables rule and flip tcp_mtu_probing back to 0.

ben: Watch out for IPv6-only clients behind weird consumer CPEs — clamp too low impacts throughput. 1220 seems safe.

maya: Thanks all. Canaries scheduled. Will report back in ~1h after rollout. :thumbsup: :eyes:
